clue.text: Landing ground needs helium for large computer

parts.note: HE is the chemical symbol for helium
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an iPad is Apple's tablet computer

explanation.surface: A spaceport or airfield requires helium in exchange for a big computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad where helicopters touch down is a small landing ground for rotor aircraft.

clue.text: Trusty hen's first over place to hatch eggs

indicators.note: first here picks the opening letter of the word hen's

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
birds hatch their eggs in a nest

explanation.surface: A reliable hen takes priority over the nesting site.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty and honest both describe someone reliable and truthful.

clue.text: 8 at which siren destroyed ships

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, a north–south position on the globe, is abbreviated L

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of siren are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A siren lured vessels to ruin at a certain point on the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' turns SIREN into INERS; L, the abbreviation for the answer to 8 down, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Liners are large passenger vessels, such as ocean-going cruise ships.

clue.text: Beginning of popular poem by Welsh conservative writer

indicators.note: beginning of picks the first letter of popular

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or ballad
the political right is conservative

explanation.surface: The start of a well-liked poem by a right-wing Welsh author.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays, so is a kind of writer.

clue.text: Terrible setting for end of boring requiem

indicators.note: setting for means the word for terrible is a mount that holds the letter, like a jewel's setting

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of boring

explanation.surface: A dreadful arrangement for the close of a tedious mass for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, as a requiem is.

clue.text: Pastry with extremely sweet, coarse caramel base

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes of the word sweet, its first and last letters

parts.note: coarse, as in vulgar, means rude

indicators.note: base points to the bottom of the word caramel, its final letter

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: pastry on a very sweet, rough caramel base.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered Austrian pastry, usually filled with apple.

clue.text: Replace foreign reps wearing soft leather fabric

indicators.note: wearing means the leather goes round the jumbled letters, like clothes on a body

parts.note: suede is soft napped leather

indicators.note: foreign means the letters of reps are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Swap out overseas sales representatives dressed in suede.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' pictures the leather fabric worn around the rearranged letters; 'foreign' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to take the place of something older, to supplant it.

clue.text: Breeze from the south crossing German capital

indicators.note: crossing means the reversed word straddles the letter for German
in a down clue, from the south means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a breeze is moving air

explanation.surface: A southerly wind blows across the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' reverses AIR to RIA; 'crossing' puts G inside it. The surface points to Berlin, but G is the only German part.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Cop given nuts spitting out large stones

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector, a police officer

indicators.note: spitting out means one letter is expelled from the nuts

parts.note: almonds are nuts

explanation.surface: A police officer eating nuts spits out some big stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds are precious gemstones, often just called stones by jewellers.

clue.text: Allowance got by lecturer before head of technology leaves position

indicators.note: before means the lecturer's letter comes first
leaves says one letter departs from the word for position

parts.note: an attitude is a position or posture

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of technology

explanation.surface: A lecturer's allowance was obtained ahead of the tech chief quitting a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is freedom or scope allowed, room to act as one chooses.

clue.text: Japanese assassin held in Benin jail

indicators.note: held in says the answer is kept inside the words Benin jail, running across them

explanation.surface: A Japanese hitman is locked up in a West African prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents of feudal Japan, hired for espionage and killing.

clue.text: Nasty man leaving those left behind to protect dog

indicators.note: to protect means the shortened word wraps round and shields the dog
leaving says the letter for man departs from the word for those left behind

parts.note: a remnant is what remains, those left behind
M is the abbreviation for male, so man
a pug is a small flat-faced breed of dog

explanation.surface: A vile fellow walks out on the survivors, but guards the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' gives M, as in the abbreviation for male; 'leaving' removes it and 'to protect' wraps what is left round the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant and nasty are synonyms: both describe something offensive or distasteful.

clue.text: New brewery tsar dismissing English version of fruity beer

indicators.note: New signals the letters being made into something new, a fresh arrangement
dismissing means one letter is sent away from the letters of brewery tsar before rearranging

explanation.surface: A fresh brewing boss scraps the English take on a fruit-flavoured ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes one E from BREWERYTSAR, and 'New' rearranges the remaining ten letters; 'version of' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers brewed with soft summer berries are sold under that fruit's name, so the word names one fruit-flavoured ale.

clue.text: Type of water bath

definitions.meaning: in printing, a typeface or set of type characters is a ...
the basin of holy water in a church used for baptism

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a typeface in printing and the church basin used for baptisms.

clue.text: Turned on cash register containing note with forged date

indicators.note: containing means the till holds the note inside it

parts.note: a till is a cash register
ti is the seventh note in sol-fa

indicators.note: forged means the letters of date are faked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cash register was switched on holding a banknote with a fake date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is the sol-fa syllable, not a banknote; 'containing' puts it inside the register and 'forged' rearranges the date.
explanation.definitionFit: Being titillated is being excited or aroused, turned on.

clue.text: Inclined not to marry

parts.note: read literally, someone minded to stay unwed has a mind set on staying unmarried; the real sense is determined or focused

explanation.surface: Someone disposed to remain a bachelor or spinster.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means resolutely focused on one aim; the clue reads it as having a mind set on staying unwed.

clue.text: See 23
Write to male exposed as love cheat

indicators.note: exposed suggests the letters laid bare and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Writing to a man unmasked as an unfaithful lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who two-times is unfaithful, dating two partners at once.

clue.text: Instrument at home in dark red cover

indicators.note: cover means the dark red wraps around the phrase for at home

parts.note: claret is a dark red colour, from the wine
in means at home

explanation.surface: An instrument at home under a dark red case.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Run away without paying for excellent piece of cheesy snack

parts.note: to welsh is to dodge paying a debt, especially a bet
rare can mean excellent, as in a rare old time
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Dodging the bill for a fine portion of something cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: WELSH RAREBIT is cheese sauce on toast, a British snack.
explanation.definitionFit: This dish is melted seasoned cheese poured over toast, a savoury snack.

clue.text: Writer cries afresh about book

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the letter for book
afresh means the letters of cries are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer weeps anew over a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe copies or writes documents, so is a writer.

clue.text: Devotional songs sung by priest and son getting donations for the needy

parts.note: alms are gifts of charity to the poor

explanation.surface: Hymns sung by a cleric and his son while collecting for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms are the sacred songs of the Bible's Book of Psalms, sung in worship.

clue.text: Twist lid of tea container

indicators.note: the lid sits at the top, so lid of picks the first letter of tea

parts.note: an urn is a container, as for tea in a café

explanation.surface: Twist the top off a tea caddy.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something round is to rotate it, as with a knob.

clue.text: Remembers spiritual lessons with short prayers

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
a collect is a short prayer in Anglican and Catholic liturgy

explanation.surface: Religious studies lessons accompanied by brief prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLECTS is stressed on the first syllable here: short set prayers in the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to call something back to mind, to recall.

clue.text: Eager to join TV phone-in broadcast via the bush telegraph

indicators.note: broadcast means the letters are scattered about, like seed, into a new order

explanation.surface: Keen to call into a television show, passing word along by rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the fourteen letters of EAGER and TV PHONE-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing news informally, by rumour or gossip, is getting it through the bush telegraph.

clue.text: Addict's escort has no heroin

indicators.note: has no means the letter for heroin is missing from the escort

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug addict's companion is clean of heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is someone who takes drugs, an addict.

clue.text: Setter taking risk dancing in sweet garment

indicators.note: in places the setter and the jumbled letters inside the word for a sweet

parts.note: a mint is a sweet, a confection
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of risk moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler daringly dances inside a sweet clothing item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the compiler's I; 'dancing' rearranges risk, and 'in' places both inside the sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniskirt is a very short skirt, an item of women's clothing.

clue.text: Drawer behind counter containing wide fabric

indicators.note: containing says the drawer holds the letter for wide inside it

parts.note: a till is the cash drawer behind a shop counter
W is the abbreviation for wide, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A shop drawer under the counter holding a broad length of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a cloth woven with diagonal ribs, such as denim or gabardine.

clue.text: One who's left work about to go to Scottish island

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.surface: A pensioner is about to holiday on a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has stopped their career has left work for good.

clue.text: Non-stop part of pretend lesson

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A make-believe class that never seems to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a finish continues without pause, never stopping.
